hook.text: A telephone line carries voices. A fiber optic cable carries Netflix. The difference is bandwidth.

buildup.text: Bandwidth is the range of frequencies a channel can transmit. Wider bandwidth means more data per second.

discovery.text: Human speech needs about 4 kHz. HD video needs millions of times more. Each application has bandwidth demands.

twist.text: Bandwidth is finite and expensive. Every wireless device competes for the same limited radio spectrum.

climax.text: Compression, multiplexing, and clever encoding squeeze more information into less bandwidth every year.

punchline.text: Wider pipe, more data. But pipes aren't free.

quiz.question: What does bandwidth measure?
options: The range of frequencies a channel can carry
The physical size of a cable
